subject: Billing entity mapping & GST withholding — invoice split needed
messages:
From: Aisha Raman <aisha.raman@paybridge.co>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts@paybridge.co
Date: 2026-09-27T09:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Billing entity / GST question

Hi Ben —

Hope you're well. Our AP team reviewed the draft invoice and flagged two items before we can process payment: 1) PayBridge is required to withhold GST for services billed to our India entity unless the supplier can confirm reverse-charge applicability; and 2) our system needs the supplier's registered tax entity name and GSTIN on the invoice header.

Can Redwood confirm which legal entity the invoice will be issued from (Redwood Inference Inc. vs Redwood EU Ltd) and whether you can provide an entity declaration (or split the invoice) so our pay team can avoid incorrectly applying withholding?

We've attached the AP form we normally ask suppliers to fill out. If splitting the invoice is easier, we can accept two invoices — one to PayBridge Global (no GST withholding) and one to PayBridge India with withholding applied.

Thanks,
Aisha
Accounts Payable — PayBridge
attachments: ap-entity-form.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Raman <aisha.raman@paybridge.co>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Billing entity / GST question

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the heads up and the form. Quick answers up front: Redwood can issue invoices from either Redwood Inference, Inc. (US) or Redwood Inference EU Ltd (Ireland). We also support issuing a split invoice (two invoices) if that works for your workflow.

Before I route to finance to prepare the documents, two quick clarifications so we don't go back and forth:
- Can you confirm the legal pay-to name and GSTIN for the India entity? (It looks like PayBridge India Pvt Ltd in your AP system, but I want to be sure.)
- Which entity on your side will be responsible for tax withholding? (If PayBridge India pays locally, they will need the GSTIN on the India invoice.)

I'll attach our supplier entity-declaration template and a proposed split we can generate for you. Lauren / Vanessa — can you pick which billing entity (US vs EU vs split) gives us the cleanest tax outcome for Redwood? My preference is to avoid withholding where allowed, but we can accommodate a split.

Cheers,
Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: entity-declaration-form.docx, proposed-invoice-split-draft.pdf

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T09:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Billing entity / GST question

Ben —

Looping in our billing lead, Vanessa (copied), but initial tax notes:
- If the contracting entity is Redwood Inference EU Ltd and the service is consumed by an Indian branch of PayBridge, reverse-charge usually doesn't apply — India GST reverse-charge rules are narrow and often require local registration.
- To avoid PayBridge withholding, we can issue the services invoice to PayBridge Global (non-India entity) from Redwood Inference, Inc. or EU Ltd depending on contractual terms — but please confirm the procuring/legal entity on their purchase order.
- If PayBridge insists the India entity will be the payer, prepare for potential 2%–5% withholding depending on nature of services and local guidance; we'll need to clearly mark GSTINs.

Vanessa — can finance prepare two candidate invoices: (A) single invoice to PayBridge Global (no GSTIN on header), (B) split invoice with line items allocated to PayBridge India (include our GSTIN placeholder) and PayBridge Global? I'll include the supplier declaration they sent for our records.

Lauren
Head of Revenue Ops

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Raman <aisha.raman@paybridge.co>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T11:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Billing entity / GST question

Hi Aisha / Ben / Lauren —

Thanks — Vanessa from Billing here. We've prepared a proposed split and a single-invoice option and attached both. Notes:
- Option 1 (single invoice): Bill to PayBridge Global Ltd; Redwood issues from Redwood Inference EU Ltd. No India GSTIN on header. This avoids local withholding provided PayBridge Global is the contracting party.
- Option 2 (split invoice): Two invoices — 70% to PayBridge Global (EU invoice) and 30% to PayBridge India Pvt Ltd (IN invoice). The India invoice will include Redwood's Indian GST placeholder (we need to confirm if Redwood has local registration; currently we do not). Without local registration, we can still issue the invoice but PayBridge may be required to apply withholding.

To proceed with Option 2 we need: 1) Completed supplier entity-declaration form (attached) with your India GSTIN and legal pay-to name; 2) Confirmation PayBridge India will accept an invoice that may have withholding applied.

If you'd like, we can also issue Option 2 with a tax note: "Tax withheld at source by the payer as per Indian GST rules" so your AP system will map it.

Attachments: proposed-invoice-split.pdf, entity-declaration-form.docx

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Billing Manager — Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Raman <aisha.raman@paybridge.co>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T15:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Billing entity / GST question

Thanks, Vanessa — that's helpful.

We can accept Option 2 (split) provided Redwood completes the declaration and confirms the exact wording for the tax note so our AP mapping picks up withheld amounts correctly. Our India entity is "PayBridge India Pvt Ltd" with GSTIN: 27AAAA0000A1Z5 (this is the company GSTIN). We'll complete the supplier form and attach it by Friday.

Action items for Redwood:
- Confirm whether Redwood has an Indian GSTIN or will provide an invoice that acknowledges potential withholding.
- Provide the exact tax-note string you prefer us to map (e.g., "Tax withheld at source – Indian GST as per Sec XYZ") so we can add it as a mapping rule.

We'll get the supplier form back to you by 2026-10-09. If Redwood doesn't have Indian GST registration, we'll proceed with split invoice + withholding on the India portion.

Thanks,
Aisha
Accounts Payable — PayBridge
attachments: completed-ap-acknowledgement.pdf (to follow)
